## Background 

There are many *graphic systems* in R for amking plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**. 

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems:

We can use the in-built `cars` dataset:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

A base R plot:

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**
 Before I can use ggplot2 I need to install it on my computer. To do this we can use the function `install.packages("ggplot2")`

> **N.D** We never run an `install.packages()` in our quarto doc (we run it in our R concole) as it would re-install the package every time I render my document. 


Once installed we still need to load it up into our R session. We do this with `libary()` call

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs:

- the **data** (a data.frame of the stuff we want to plot)
- the **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot)
- the **geom** layer (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point()
```

## Lets add some features (more layers)

Lets add a trend line that shows the relationship bewteen `speed` and `distance`

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() 
```

Now to clean up the ``geo_smooth()``

```{r}
ggplot(cars) + 
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)", y="Stopping Distance (ft)" , title= "Stopping distance in some old cars")
```

## Gene Expression Plot

Frist we will read some expression data for the effects of a GLP-1 drug

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```
Now for the ``ggplot()``

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() 
```

Now to clean up the ``ggplot()``

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("blue","gray","red")) +
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Control (no drug)", y="Drug Treatment" , title= "Gene Expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment")
```

```{r}
nrow(genes)
colnames(genes)
ncol(genes)
table(genes$State)
round( table(genes$State)/nrow(genes) * 100, 2 )
sum(genes$State=="up") / nrow(genes) *100
round(2.444188,2)
```


## Going Further

Here we read the famous *gapmider*

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many different "country" values are in this dataset?

```{r}
length( unique(gapminder$country))
```

Useful ``Functions``:
- nrow()
- table()
- unique()
- length()


Lets make our first plot of `gdpPercap` vs `lifeExp` :

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.25)
```

One useful layer we can add to explore big datasets like this is called **facetting**

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

### Limit to 1977 and 2007

We can install and use **dplyr** package to help us "filter" the full dataset down to a smaller subset that only includes the years I want.

First we need to run 'install.packages(dplyr)' and then load it with 'library(dplyr)'.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

filter(gapminder, year==2007, country== "United States")
#gapminder$year 
```

> Q. Make a histogram of lifeExp fil color by contenient

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_histogram(alpha=1)
```

> Q. Now for a boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha=1)
```
